info.name: Revenue Metrics Service
info.description:
One canonical collected-revenue metric across Stripe, PayPal and a CSV ledger, exposed through two views that cannot disagree.

Set the `baseUrl` variable to switch between the deployed service and a local one.

NOTES
- `to` is EXCLUSIVE. A range covering all of July is from=2026-07-01&to=2026-08-01.
- All bucketing is UTC.
- `amountMinor` is integer minor units in a STRING. Totals here exceed Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so parsing to a float loses precision.
- The free Render instance sleeps when idle; the first request after a pause takes ~50s. Call Health first.

item.name: 0. Health — wakes the instance, states the definition

request.description: Cheap DB round-trip plus the canonical definition. 200 when Postgres answers, 503 when it does not. Run this first — the free tier spins down when idle.
Every route, plus the definition and the range semantics.
Total collected revenue per currency. The USD figure is above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER — that is the BIGINT path carrying a real value, which is why amounts are serialized as strings.

item.name: 3. Daily — the same number, per UTC day

request.description: Summing `days` per currency reproduces the summary exactly. Both views are built from one shared SQL clause factory and differ only by a date_trunc grouping key, so agreement is by construction rather than by test.

item.name: 4. Daily — one week (small enough to read on screen)
5. Unmapped — what the allow-list kept OUT

request.description: Statuses no adapter recognised (`disputed`, `on_hold`), with the amount each held out of revenue. An exclusion list such as `status != 'failed'` would have counted all of it. Excluding an unknown status is only safe if somebody finds out it appeared.
Idempotent upsert on (source, external_id). Run it twice — `fetched`/`upserted` show real work, and the revenue totals do not move.
PayPal's Transaction Search lags up to 3 hours, so the adapter never queries or advances its watermark past now-3h. `fetched: 0` means caught up, not broken.
Returns 207 when some sources succeeded and others failed, so failures are not hidden behind a 200.

item.name: 9. Demo — create Stripe charges (does NOT sync)

request.description:
Creates real test-mode charges and stops. Two of the five are deliberately not revenue: a declined card and a fully refunded charge. Both are genuinely in Stripe and neither ever reaches the total.

Run 6 (Sync Stripe) next, then 2 (Summary) — the number moves by the collected charges only. count is 1-5; a 10s cooldown returns 429.
400. Rejected rather than silently swapped — silent swapping is a correctness bug wearing a convenience costume.
400. new Date('2026-02-30') rolls forward to March 2nd rather than failing, so the parser compares an ISO round-trip instead.
400 UNKNOWN_SOURCE, listing the sources that are registered.
200 with empty totals, empty sources, and no days. No crash, no null.
